meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мница'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'clever person, good girl/boy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот и умница, работа лечит всё!

examples.trans: You are a real clever girl, dear niece.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to prepare, to cook, to make
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least, just', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'champagne' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там же президент выступает! Надо открыть шампанское.
examples.trans: But the president is on TV! We have to open the champagne.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing; piece' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А жизнь — сложная штука. Вы понимаете, о чём я?
examples.trans: And life is a complicated thing. Do you understand what I am talking about?
And life is a complicated thing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'by the way; handy', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from, out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'cabbage; cash (slang)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая капуста.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new cabbage.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to lay down', paired with 'класть'.

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

examples.text: А вот сюда я её и положу! Отличный подарок будет!
examples.trans: Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'nose' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Когда не можешь сам себе нос вытереть.
examples.trans: When you can't even wipe your own nose yourself.

examples.text: От холода у него покраснел нос.
examples.trans: His nose turned red from the cold.

examples.text: У меня скоро долгожданная пенсия на носу.
examples.trans: My long-awaited pension is right around the corner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, later, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'суда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'dishes, tableware, crockery' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Get up and go wash the dishes!
Clean tableware is on the table.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'next; further', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to beat, to hit', paired with 'побить'.

examples.text: Почему меня все бьют в этом доме?
examples.trans: Why does everyone beat me in this house?

examples.text: Тише, Ваня, осторожно! Зачем ты бьёшь дерево ногой?
examples.trans: Easy, Vanya, be careful! Why are you kicking the tree with your foot?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it.

examples.text: Да ерунда, мне даже нравится. Как тебе твой новый кандидат?
examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it. How do you like your new candidate?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'happiness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: How much money is needed for happiness?

examples.text: Сколько миллионов нужно человеку для счастья?
examples.trans: How many millions does a person need for happiness?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Common masculine noun meaning 'dad' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'grass, herb; (slang) weed' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned.

examples.text: Весной в парке растёт зелёная трава.
examples.trans: Green grass grows in the park in spring.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to eat', paired with 'съесть'.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!
